entries.title: Eos: a merger-induced starburst at the dawn of Galactic low-$α$ disc formation
entries.abstract: The last significant merger of the Milky Way, the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GS/E), is thought to have reshaped the early Galaxy and to mark the transition from the high-$α$ to the low-$α$ disc. The stars formed in situ during this merger offer a direct record of that epoch but are hard to identify. Using APOGEE DR17 abundances, we study Eos, a population of in-situ low-$α$ stars on halo-like, non-rotating, eccentric orbits. The metal-poor part of Eos has a nitrogen dispersion as large as that of the pre-disc Aurora population and up to 1.7 times that of the low-$α$ disc at the same metallicity. Heating alone cannot produce this: the Splash, a disc heated onto halo orbits by the same merger and selected in the same way, shows no excess over its parent disc. This part of Eos was therefore born in poorly mixed gas. Eos is also chemically intermediate between the accreted GS/E debris and the coeval in-situ Milky Way stars, and stars with more GS/E-like chemistry move on more extended orbits. Its stars are older than the bulk of the low-$α$ disc but younger than the high-$α$ disc and the Splash. We compare these observations with a merger-induced starburst seen in an Auriga simulation. There, a GS/E-like merger funnels the stripped progenitor gas into a mixing lane of intermediate metallicity, where stars form with intermediate abundances, a large chemical dispersion and a chemodynamical gradient set by their birth site, reproducing the observed signatures of Eos. We therefore interpret Eos as the surviving relic of the GS/E merger-induced starburst, born largely from the partially mixed gas bridging the two galaxies and marking the onset of the Milky Way's low-$α$ disc. Eos thus provides a direct observational view of the star formation and galaxy evolution driven by the Milky Way's last significant merger.

entries.title: The OGLE Collection of Variable Stars. Over 1.3 Million Human-Verified Eclipsing and Ellipsoidal Binaries in the Milky Way
entries.abstract: We present a new release of the OGLE collection of eclipsing and ellipsoidal binary systems in the Galactic bulge and disk. The catalog contains 1 330 024 objects, including 1 280 765 eclipsing binaries and 49 259 ellipsoidal variables, nearly three times as many systems as the previous editions of the OGLE collection. The selection and classification process involved expert visual inspection of the light curves. The catalog incorporates all available OGLE-II, OGLE-III, and OGLE-IV photometry, extending the observational baseline to nearly 28 years for some objects. The orbital periods and other observational parameters of previously known systems have been updated. We present basic statistics of the sample and highlight selected rare and unusual systems.

entries.title: Top-heavy Initial Mass Functions are not enough at cosmic dawn
entries.abstract: A top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) has been proposed to explain the unexpected abundance of ultraviolet (UV)-bright galaxies at cosmic dawn. We test this possibility using the metallicity-dependent, top-heavy IMF recently proposed by Chon et al. (2024), which is motivated by simulations of metal-poor star formation. We compare this IMF with a Salpeter IMF, self-consistently including the associated changes in UV emission, supernova feedback, metal enrichment, and dust production. At fixed star formation rate, the Chon IMF enhances the intrinsic UV luminosity by a factor ${B}_{1500}\simeq4.7$-$2.8$ over halo masses $M_h=10^{8-12}\,M_\odot$. However, its larger supernova rate suppresses star formation and increases dust attenuation, reducing the net boost to ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq2.0$-$1.06$. For halos relevant to the bright end of the UV luminosity function, the enhancement is only ${B}_{\rm UV}\simeq1.2$-$1.4$, or about $0.3$ mag. Calculations with the DELPHI semi-analytic model confirm that the self-consistent Chon and Salpeter UV luminosity functions differ by less than $0.5$ dex at $z\simeq11$-$17$. Thus, a top-heavy IMF alone cannot explain the bright galaxy excess. Conversely, the predicted pair-instability supernova abundance differs by factors of $2$-$6$ between the two IMFs, providing a potentially cleaner observational diagnostic of the high-mass stellar populations at these early epochs.

entries.title: Influence of variable IMF on the dynamical black hole mass estimates in massive ETGs
entries.abstract: Several studies have shown that the stellar initial mass function (IMF) in massive early-type galaxies (ETGs) is not universal. Recent results from stellar population synthesis models, based on integral-field unit (IFU) observations, indicate that the IMF varies radially, becoming increasingly bottom-heavy towards galaxy centres. This radial variation alters the stellar mass-to-light ratio ($\rm M_{*}/L$) and can significantly affect dynamical black hole (BH) mass estimates in massive ETGs. In this study, we investigate the impact of a radially varying IMF on BH mass estimates for five massive galaxies: NGC3923, NGC4261, NGC4636, IC4296, and IC4329. Using DYNAMITE, a triaxial Schwarzschild orbit-based modelling code, we perform mass modelling of these galaxies based on MUSE and SINFONI IFU observations. Our models incorporate radially varying stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$ profiles derived from spatially resolved stellar population modelling with a free IMF, and we compare the resulting BH masses with those obtained from dynamical models assuming a constant stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$. All galaxies in our sample show bottom-heavy IMFs in their central regions, with the IMF generally becoming lighter towards larger radii. We obtain constrained BH masses for NGC3923 and IC4329, while only upper limits are obtained for NGC4261, NGC4636, and IC4296. Compared with the constant-$\rm M_{*}/L$ models, the variable-$\rm M_{*}/L$ models yield BH masses lower by approximately 83% and 11% for NGC3923 and IC4329, respectively, while the BH mass upper limits for the other galaxies can increase or decrease. Our results demonstrate that spatial variations in the IMF and stellar $\rm M_{*}/L$ can have a non-negligible but strongly galaxy-dependent impact on dynamical BH mass measurements. These results highlight the importance of accounting for such variations in future dynamical modelling efforts.

entries.title: Twisted resonant orbits: Quantifying the deceleration of the Galactic bar
entries.abstract: Recent structural discoveries in Gaia Data Release 3 reveal distinct, chevron-shaped over-densities in the radial phase space of the halo. Although initial interpretations identify these features as the phase-mixed relics of a past galaxy merger, their prominent asymmetry and persistence at high metallicities strongly challenge this interpretation. These features are better explained as a dynamical response to a Galactic bar, where stars are trapped in resonances. We establish the fractional $v_r$ asymmetry of the chevrons as a quantitative diagnostic tool for the bar's rotational state. We utilise test-particle simulations of a Milky Way-like galaxy to model various bar pattern speed evolutions, including decelerating and constant speed scenarios. By mapping the fractional asymmetry of the phase-space chevrons across a parameter space of bar deceleration rates and pattern speeds, we establish a direct correlation between the bar's deceleration and the rotational response of the resonant orbits. Comparing these simulated constraints with observational data from Gaia DR3 provides a framework for measuring the current deceleration of the Galactic bar, and a probe of the amount of dynamical friction occurring between the baryonic and dark matter content of the Milky Way. We find a dimensionless deceleration parameter $η\equiv - \dotΩ_b/Ω_b^2 = 0.0015^{+0.0016}_{-0.0009}$, equivalent to $\dotΩ_b = -2.23^{+1.50}_{-2.46} \, \text{km s}^{-1} \text{kpc}^{-1} \text{Gyr}^{-1}$, in agreement with previous estimates obtained with independent methods. Gaia DR4 should sharpen this measurement considerably.

entries.title: Subsolar neutron star-black hole binaries from collapsars: Gravitational waveform models and detectability in current searches
entries.abstract: Detecting subsolar objects in binary mergers would be an exceptional discovery in gravitational wave astronomy. So far, dedicated searches for subsolar coalescences reported no confident detections, setting upper bounds on their merger rate. Given that standard stellar evolution is not able to produce subsolar candidates, a confident detection would point either to new physics or to unconventional astrophysical pathways. These include collapsars, where the outer parts of neutrino-cooled accretion disks around newborn stellar-mass black holes are subject to fragmentation and give rise to subsolar neutron stars, which can later merge with the central black hole. We show that current subsolar searches may miss a significant fraction of these neutron star-black hole mergers, because their templates do not account for the small mass ratios, the tidal disruption of the neutron star, and the effects of the surrounding gas. This result motivates improving the waveform modeling used in current subsolar searches and building adequate template banks tailored to these systems.

entries.title: Ram Pressure Is Unable to Strip All Phases of the Interstellar Medium out of Spirals Falling into Galaxy Clusters
entries.abstract: Following the expansion of the Universe, spiral galaxies may fall at large speeds into galaxy clusters. Their interaction with the intracluster medium (ICM) may remove part of their gas and reduce their capacity for making new stars, as envisaged by Gunn & Gott. Ram pressure stripping (RPS) is commonly invoked to explain this gas loss and the wakes or tails left behind in-falling galaxies. Here we revise the impact of RPS on individual dense clouds and particularly focus on turbulent viscous stripping (TVS), driven by Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities at the cloud-ICM interface, that affects the high-density and low-temperature molecular gas. For an extended gaseous body to decelerate, momentum from its exposed surface must be communicated into the gas by a hydrodynamic disturbance able to propagate through it. Three-dimensional hydrodynamic calculations follow this interaction with dense clouds. At cloud number densities $n_{\mathrm{cl}}=10^2$ cm$^{-3}$, ram pressure acting through the transmitted shock strongly compresses and deforms the cloud and produces only a small deceleration; at $n_{\mathrm{cl}}=10^3$ cm$^{-3}$, the slower transmitted shock produces much weaker deformation. At both cloud densities, TVS continuously removes gas from the cloud surface and forms qualitatively indistinguishable trailing wakes, with comparable mass-loss rates, suggesting that TVS acting on individual dense clouds can generate filamentary substructure within jellyfish-galaxy tails.

entries.title: Kinetic Tomography with Diffuse Interstellar Bands in APOGEE DR17
entries.abstract: Context: Mapping gas flows in the interstellar medium is key to understanding the formation of structure in our Milky Way. Methods that simultaneously reconstruct clouds' distances and line-of-sight velocities are called kinetic tomography (KT). Diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) are powerful tracers for such maps because they trace the integrated dust density and the dust-weighted velocity. Previous DIB-KT works had small samples with coarse kpc-scale resolution and could not capture vertical disk structure. Aims: Make 4D (3D position + radial velocity) maps of the Milky Way from new, high-quality 15,273 Å DIB detections in APOGEE DR17. Methods: We combine variational inference and Gaussian processes with a mixture likelihood for low signal-to-noise detections and marginalization over distance uncertainties. We calibrate the model on mock fields and spectral injection tests and validate the map against independent tracers of the dust density (3D dust maps) and velocity substructure (masers and young stellar clusters). Results: We recover a posterior distribution over 3D maps of the density and velocity structure of the 15,273 Å DIB within 6 kpc of the Sun. We measure the large-scale structure of the DIB disk (scale length, height and flare) and detect vertical distortions consistent with the warp. On smaller scales, the map resolves distance ambiguities in gas longitude-velocity diagrams. From the second-order velocity structure function, we measure a slope (0.64 $\pm$ 0.04) consistent with Kolmogorov turbulence, amplitude consistent with expectations for molecular clouds, and a preliminary ratio of compressive-to-solenoidal modes. Conclusions: With larger DIB catalogs expected from SDSS-V, this framework should resolve kinematic substructure at the scales needed to constrain the formation and dynamics of individual clouds and voids. (abridged)

entries.title: Off-Nuclear AGN Signatures in MaNGA: Spatially resolved selection using MEGACUBES
entries.abstract: We present a spatially resolved search for off-nuclear active galactic nucleus (AGN) candidates in the MaNGA survey. Using megacubes, we analyze over 10,000 galaxies, separating AGN activity from diffuse ionized gas with refined equivalent-width and surface-brightness thresholds. Combining a spatial radial algorithm with BPT, WHaN, and WHaD diagnostics, we classify 261 nuclear AGNs, 201 off-nuclear AGNs, and 159 'quiet' (composite-spaxel-dominated) sources. We test whether off-nuclear AGNs reside in distinct host galaxies or whether the offset is a local, gas-driven phenomenon. Nuclear and off-nuclear AGN hosts are statistically indistinguishable in stellar mass, age, star formation rate, and gas-phase metallicity. However, the excitation and kinematics of the AGN-ionized gas differ significantly: nuclear AGN spaxels have [O III]$\lambda5007$ luminosities $\sim 0.7$ dex higher than off-nuclear spaxels, whose lower [O III]/H$β$ ratios indicate genuinely lower-excitation gas rather than an obscured view of the central engine. We also find an orientation trend: 72% of nuclear hosts are face-on, versus 50% of off-nuclear hosts, so projection effects contribute to, but do not fully explain, off-nuclear detections. The classical WHaN boundary at $\log$([N II]/H$α$) = -0.4 misclassifies high-metallicity diffuse ionized gas in integral field data; an empirical shift to -0.25 removes over 48,000 spurious AGN spaxels. Finally, the off-nuclear fraction implies an episodic AGN phase lifetime of $\sim 5 \times 10^4$ yr, consistent within a factor of a few with independent fading-AGN estimates and supporting short, recurrent accretion bursts.

entries.title: Spiral Pitch Angles in Black Hole Images and Movies
entries.abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has produced images of M87* and Sgr A*, and will soon produce time sequences of images, or movies. General relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) models predict EHT sources will exhibit brightness fluctuations along the ring. The fluctuations are commonly connected to trailing spiral features. Here, we introduce a method to measure the pitch angle $ψ$ of radially extended features by cross-correlating brightness fluctuations sampled on rings at two distinct impact parameters. Pitch angle can be reliably measured from synthetic movies with BHEX resolution, and can be constrained even at EHT resolution. Single images enable noisy constraints of $ψ$. Pitch angle depends most on the viewing inclination and black hole spin. For constant inclination, the spiral winding direction depends on the sign of spin, with spirals winding more tightly in the direction of frame dragging near the horizon. The pitch angle will complement other observables to reliably constrain both the source inclination and spin in future analysis by EHT, and by expansions to the EHT such as ngEHT and BHEX.

entries.title: A novel pathway to stellar-mass black hole growth: Re-accretion of gas from stellar wind bubbles
entries.abstract: The formation of high-mass stellar black holes (BHs) observed in mergers by gravitational wave observatories remains difficult to explain using standard models of stellar evolution. We investigate whether newly formed stellar-mass BHs in dense molecular clouds can significantly increase their final mass by accreting gas from pre-existing, wind-blown interstellar bubbles produced by their progenitor stars. We performed 1D and 3D hydrodynamic simulations of interstellar bubbles driven by stellar feedback, incorporating thermal conduction, radiative cooling, gravity, ionizing radiation, stellar winds, and supernova (SN) explosions. We modeled the subsequent accretion onto the central BH for two formation scenarios: core-collapse SN and direct collapse. Our parameter space study encompasses over 500 1D simulations, varying initial cloud densities, gravitational binding energies, progenitor masses ($40-257\,M_\odot$), and metallicities ($0.66\,Z_\odot$ and $0.016\,Z_\odot$), and tracks the bubble evolution for millions of years post-BH formation. Scenarios exhibiting significant re-accretion were further validated using high-resolution 3D simulations. Our simulations show that BHs formed via direct collapse from low-metallicity progenitors can accrete up to $6.9\,M_\odot$ of gas from massive inner shells formed by late-stage slow winds, resulting in final BH masses of up to $93\,M_\odot$. Conversely, we find no significant re-accretion in scenarios involving an SN explosion or high-metallicity progenitors; in these cases, fast winds or SN ejecta efficiently evacuate dense structures from the bubble interior, leaving behind a hot, low-density medium. [abridged] This mechanism may help explain the unexpectedly high masses of BHs observed in gravitational wave events.

entries.title: On the High Eccentricity Orbit of 51 Eri b and Constraints on Interactions with a Second Companion
entries.abstract: The eccentricity of an exoplanet's orbit is a key observational quantity that can be used to infer its dynamical past and predict its future orbital evolution. Planets are expected to emerge from their protoplanetary cradles with roughly circular eccentricities, and non-circular eccentricites to arise from subsequent dynamical processing in the absence of the gas disk. We present an updated orbit for 51 Eridani b based on 5 years of 0.2 mas precision optical interferometry from VLTI/GRAVITY(+). This planet is young (${\sim}20\,\mathrm{Myr}$ old), temperate ($T_{\rm eff}\sim650\,\mathrm{K}$), and on a wide orbit ($a{=}9.36\,\mathrm{au}$) with an uncertain mass ($M_{\rm b}\leq12\,M_{\rm J}$). We measured the planet's motion to an exceptionally high precision, confirming that its orbit is very eccentric ($e_b=0.574\pm0.003$). We observe residuals to the absolute astrometry of the host star based on a single planet orbit that could be attributable to reflex motion from a third body in the system. We construct a two companion orbit model that could explain the apparent reflex motion of 51 Eri A: this model predicts that the putative second companion has $M_c\in[1.0, 2900]_{95\%}\,M_{\rm Jup}$ and $a_c\in[0.3, 3.1]_{95\%}\,\mathrm{au}$. In this framework, a dynamical interaction between b and ``c" could have kicked the exterior, lower mass b out onto its present, eccentric orbit. If this signal is astrophysical, and not due to a systematic error, this candidate should be confirmable with Gaia DR4 epoch astrometry in the near future.

entries.title: Intra-day variability of the gamma-ray/optical emission of 3C 454.3: the complexity beyond the long-term correlation
entries.abstract: Simultaneous $γ$-ray/optical observations probe particle acceleration and radiative processes in blazar jets. The blazar 3C 454.3 shows a significant long-term correlation between these bands, often interpreted as support for the canonical one-zone leptonic emission model. However, both bands show strong intra-day variability, and whether the correlation persists during individual flares remains unclear. We study the $γ$-ray/optical correlation and intra-day variability of 3C 454.3 over 17 years (2007--2024), on timescales $\leq 24$ h. We analyse AGILE and Fermi-LAT observations using light curves binned from 3 to 48 h, together with simultaneous $R$-band photometry from WEBT and public optical data sets. We examine the flux and spectral evolution of individual flares, estimate time-dependent correlation properties, and derive Compton dominance from optical and $γ$-ray luminosities. We confirm the long-term correlation, but find large intrinsic dispersion and a slope of $η\simeq 1.6$--$1.7$, inconsistent with a single canonical one-zone scenario. On shorter timescales, correlation strengths range from weak to strong, with slopes spanning $η\simeq 0.4$--$2.0$. We also find orphan flares in both bands, diverse flare morphologies, distinct Compton-dominance patterns with rapid excursions from $\sim 10$ to 120, and heterogeneous spectral trends. The shortest resolved variability timescales ($t_{\rm var} \lesssim 3$ h) indicate that localized emission regions are required by causality. The $γ$-ray/optical correlation in 3C 454.3 thus arises not from a single emission regime, but from multiple epoch-dependent physical states. Increasing temporal resolution reveals richer variability, highlighting the importance of systematic intra-day, multi-epoch studies of bright FSRQs.

entries.title: Where Did the Angular Momentum Go? WASP-12 b May Have Circularized on a Retrograde Orbit
entries.abstract: WASP-12 b is the only exoplanet with confirmed orbital decay. Angular momentum transferred from its decaying orbit should have realigned the star's thin convective layer, yet an earlier Rossiter--McLaughlin (RM) measurement suggested a $\sim$60$^\circ$ spin--orbit misalignment. We present two new Keck Planet Finder RM measurements. We measure a sky-projected obliquity of $λ=-1.3\pm8.7^\circ$; and the star's projected rotation velocity is $v\sin i_\star=1.3\pm0.1~\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$, an order of magnitude lower than expected for a star of its mass and age. With WASP-12's low chromospheric activity, $\log R^\prime_{\rm HK}=-5.5$, our analysis favors an aligned system in which $v\sin i_\star$ reflects slow surface rotation with $P_{\rm rot}\sim60$ days, rather than a projection effect. Our evolution models favor a late-main-sequence star rather than a subgiant, with a central convective core found in 99\% of posterior samples. This internal structure suppresses the central-focusing and nonlinear wave-breaking mechanisms for inward-propagating gravity waves. We propose that WASP-12 b was initially placed on a retrograde orbit after high-eccentricity migration, when its host rotated at $v\sin i_\star\approx14$~km~s$^{-1}$ (or $P_{\rm rot}\sim$6 days). Tidal decay transferred orbital angular momentum to the convective envelope, aligning the surface. The retrograde interior acts as an angular-momentum reservoir, while interior--envelope coupling slows the surface rotation. A semi-empirical relation gives an envelope--interior angular-momentum exchange timescale of $\sim4$~Myr, similar to the observed orbital-decay timescale of $\sim3.25$~Myr. The angular-momentum budget also permits this initially retrograde evolution. In contrast, an initially prograde planet would have spun up the surface rotation to a rate substantially higher than observed.

entries.title: Rediscussion of eclipsing binaries. Paper 33. The A-type system CW Canis Majoris in the PLATO southern field
entries.abstract: CW CMa is a detached eclipsing binary containing two A0 V stars in a circular orbit of period 2.12 d. We analyse the light-curves of this system from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) together with published radial velocity measurements to determine the masses and radii of the component stars to high precision, obtaining masses of 2.087 +/- 0.022 Msun and 1.972 +/- 0.024 Msun, and radii of 1.841 +/- 0.012 Rsun and 1.748 +/- 0.014 Rsun. We detect a changing orbital period over the four available TESS sectors indicative of the presence of a companion on a wider orbit. We develop a new method to determine the effective temperatures of the component stars using their measured radii, the Gaia parallax, and surface-brightness calibrations to reduce the degeneracy between temperature and extinction. The method gives temperatures of 9850 +/- 280 K and 9570 +/- 270 K and an interstellar extinction of A(V) = 0.32 +/- 0.06 mag. The properties of the system can be matched by theoretical models for a subsolar metal abundance (Z = 0.010) and an age of 400 +/- 20 Myr. CW CMa has been selected as a target for the PLATO satellite, with which it will be observed for at least two years.

entries.title: Multiphase Gas in High-$z$ Cosmic Sheets
entries.abstract: We present high-resolution cosmological simulations of individual cosmic sheets ($z=3-6$) using the moving-mesh code AREPO to study cold gas ($T\approx10^4\rm ~K$) in the diffuse cosmic web. We find cosmic sheet gas forms a fragmented morphology, evident as kiloparsec-scale variations in the neutral hydrogen column density ($N_{\rm HI}$). Fragmentation arises from the bending and disruption of the cold-dense sheet core into a multiphase medium. Nonlinear thin shell instability (NTSI) and later shear-induced vorticity drive this bending, rather than previously suggested thermal or Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities. Higher resolution enhances fragmentation. Across a fourfold range in spatial resolution, $N_{\rm HI}$ covering fractions increase by factors of $\approx 1.5-3.5$ for partial Lyman-limit systems (pLLS) and Lyman-limit systems (LLS). An order-of-magnitude estimate suggests sheets may host a large fraction of the ultra-low metallicity (p)LLS population. Equivalent MP-Gadget simulations show qualitatively similar fragmentation, but numerical smoothing effects are present. Cosmic-sheet gas properties remain unconverged despite our high resolutions.

entries.title: The HI Mass Fractions of Milky Way Analog Samples
entries.abstract: We estimate average HI mass fractions, f_HI = M_HI/M_star, for nine Milky Way analog samples (MWAs): galaxies selected on similarity to the MW in terms of various properties. We find most (seven) MWAs have lower <f_HI> than a recent estimate for the MW, although only the two largest have significantly lower estimates. We suggest that either the MW has an unusual f_HI for its properties, or we are overestimating its HI content, one of many challenging global measurements to make from our perspective inside our own Galaxy.

entries.title: Transition Zone from ExoEarth to ExoVenus: Critical Insight from Planets on the Edge
entries.abstract: Venus and Earth, planets with similar masses and radii, provide astonishingly different environments, raising the question of why these two rocky worlds evolved so differently. Explaining this divergence is a central challenge in comparative planetology and astrobiology. Now, atmospheric studies of exoplanets can explore the possibilities of terrestrial planet evolution, especially in the era of JWST; however, we have not yet realized the critical insights rocky exoplanets in the Transition Zone (TZ) can provide. These TZ planets in the overlap between the Habitable Zone and Venus Zone can test how incident stellar irradiation affects surface water retention and habitability. Observations of exoplanets in the TZ can probe not only the emergence and decline of exoplanet habitability but also test hypotheses about Venus' past, complementing upcoming Venus flagship missions. Here, we analyze NASA's Exoplanet Archive, updated with Gaia DR3 data, and provide a target list of 23 rocky exoplanets in the Earth-to-Venus Transition Zone, along with 2 planets in the Venus Evolution Zone (EV). We examine their demographics and quantify their potential for follow-up observations. This list of rocky TZ and EV planets allows observers to optimize target selection and observing strategy for specific instruments. Characterizing exoplanets in the Transition Zone will be critical to investigating open questions about the emergence and decline of habitability on rocky worlds, the evolution from an exo-Earth to an exo-Venus, and Earth's future.

entries.title: Sherlock 'Chrones: The Curious Case of NGC 6791 and Asteroseismic Targets Therein Reveals Mixing Length Dependence on Evolutionary Stage
entries.abstract: As single-aged populations containing stars spanning a range of masses but otherwise with similar properties, star clusters provide valuable testbeds for stellar evolution theory. The old, metal-rich, open cluster NGC 6791 is well studied, but the availability of asteroseismic observations of individual cluster members allows for a more in-depth analysis. Driven by mounting evidence that the solar assumption for convection used in almost all 1D stellar models is not adequate, and in light of the increased precision provided by modern data and asteroseismic constraints, we built and compared custom isochrones with varying values of the convective mixing length, $α_\text{MLT}$, to two clusters with well-determined ages: NGC 6791 and the well-studied, metal-poor globular cluster M92. For both clusters, we found that the best-fitting mixing length parameter decreases monotonically as a function of evolutionary phase, finding values between $0.98-1.10α_{\odot}$ for NGC 6791 and $1.16-1.21α_{\odot}$ for M92. In NGC 6791, this corresponds to an 18% decrease in the best fitting mixing length between the main sequence turn-off and upper end of the red giant branch. The degree of variation found within this one object is therefore comparable to variation across the literature in $α_\text{MLT}$ fits for other non-solar targets, calling single-valued $α_\text{MLT}$ fits to clusters into question. It is also consistent with $\log g$-$α_\text{MLT}$ trends predicted by higher-fidelity, 3D convection analyses. Our results therefore illustrate the need for more flexibility in our treatment of the mixing length in isochrones to properly model clusters.

entries.title: 3D Binary Evolution of a Merging Binary Black Hole Progenitor
entries.abstract: Mass transfer is a highly dynamical 3D process that spans evolutionary timescales in binary stars. It is key to the production of gravitational waves through formation of binary black holes and other double compact objects. We integrate global 3D hydrodynamics into stellar evolutionary modeling to resolve mass transfer across nuclear timescales. We employ the shellular approximation in the stellar evolution code MESA to map a 3D spatial structure by equipotential shells in the Roche geometry to maintain hydrostatic equilibrium across tidally-distorted surfaces. We employ the method of time-incremented multiscale evolution to alternate between stellar evolution and 3D hydrodynamics to span large timescales with dynamical feedback. We employ this framework to examine a likely merging binary black hole progenitor system of a low-metallicity 30Msol donor star and 9.3Msol black hole from the end of the main sequence to core Carbon depletion. We modeled two complete mass transfer phases in 3D while self-consistently accounting for stellar evolution. These comprised a thermal-timescale early Case B phase and a nuclear-timescale late Case B phase. The prescription of Kolb & Ritter (1990) closely predicted the results of 3D evolution, except at the end of the first phase of mass transfer; our 3D model remained well-contained by the outer Lagrange point, despite 1D predictions of substantial L3 overflow during this stage. We find incorporating 3D hydrodynamics during Case B mass transfer did not significantly impact expected merger times. Our model never overflowed L3 as predicted by 1D prescriptions. L2/L3 outflows formed even while underflowing those equipotentials. Our model suggests these outflows can be neglected for the evolution of similar systems, but were dense enough to potentially impact X-ray observations.

entries.title: First $Ω_{\rm m}-w$ Measurement Using Only Fast Radio Burst Observations
entries.abstract: Though fast radio bursts (FRBs) are widely advocated as a dark energy probe, no valid $Ω_m-w$ constraint has been obtained exclusively from FRB data to date. Benefiting from a rapidly growing localized sample and a novel statistical framework for modeling the dispersion measure (DM), we report the first simultaneous inference of the matter density $Ω_m$ and dark energy equation of state parameter $w$ from FRBs alone, without external observational priors on these two parameters. We combine a multi-parameter emulator for the nonlinear matter power spectrum with a physically motivated electron prescription to construct a cosmology-dependent cosmic-DM distribution. Within this unified analysis framework, the mean and variance of DM respond self-consistently to the same underlying cosmology, directly connecting the FRB likelihood to both cosmic expansion and structure growth. Analyzing 125 localized FRBs at $0.105\leq z\leq2.148$, we obtain $Ω_m = 0.33^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ and $w = -0.80^{+0.28}_{-0.38}$ under the flat $w$CDM model. We find a new positive $Ω_m-w$ degeneracy in the FRB posterior, opposite to the strong anticorrelation derived from Type Ia supernovae, offering a complementary test of dark energy properties and highlighting their potential in future precision cosmological studies.

entries.title: FAST Burst-Cluster Catalog of FRB 20240114A
entries.abstract: We present the complete FAST burst-cluster catalog of FRB 20240114A, covering its 495-day active episode from January 28, 2024 to June 5, 2025. The catalog contains 13261 burst clusters, 19037 bursts, and 29026 sub-bursts detected in 99 observing sessions. The data reveal distinct organization across temporal scales. Among drifting burst clusters, downward-drifting clusters outnumber upward-drifting ones by approximately $9.4:1$. Between separate burst clusters, previously reported frequency changes show no preferred direction, while our Weibull analysis finds their arrival times broadly consistent with Poisson statistics, suggesting that burst clusters may represent approximately independent emission episodes within observing sessions. The Parkes/Murriyang observations revealed a long-term modulation of the characteristic emission frequency, and the extended FAST measurements show a consistent evolution. Burst energetics increase with cluster multiplicity and activity level, although significant scatter remains. The manually refined dispersion measure increases at $1.29\pm0.11\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}\,yr^{-1}}$, enlarging the still limited but growing sample of repeaters with increasing DM. Overall, these results summarize the spectral--temporal evolution of FRB 20240114A and present a burst-cluster catalog linked to the existing BurstID measurements, providing a basis for future studies of repeating FRBs.

entries.title: The Cosmic Infrared Background from Population III.1 Supermassive Stars and Black Holes
entries.abstract: We investigate the cosmic infrared background (CIB) that is expected to arise from the Population (Pop) III.1 supermassive black hole (SMBH) formation scenario, which involves early SMBH seeding via supermassive primordial star formation enabled by dark matter annihilation heating. We model the emission from Pop III.1 supermassive stars, including their growth phase, flash ionization phase, and early black hole accretion phase, as well as accompanying emission from lower-mass Pop III.2 stars. The CIB is composed of stellar and SMBH accretion disk continuum radiation, nebular continuum emission, and Ly$α$ radiation redistributed through scattering in the neutral intergalactic medium. Based on the feedback regulated Pop III.1 model of Petkova et al. (2026), our fiducial model assumes $\sim 10^5\,M_\odot$ Pop III.1 stars forming by $z_{\rm flash}=20$ with a comoving number density of $\sim0.2\,{\rm cMpc}^{-3}$. For this model, the combined stellar contribution is less than $1\%$ of existing direct and diffuse CIB measurements. However, the contribution to the CIB from $z\sim6-20$ SMBH accretion is expected to be larger than the Pop III.1 stellar component for average Eddington ratios $λ_{\text{Edd}} \sim 0.01$. Latest CIB observations place constraints of $λ_{\text{Edd}} \lesssim 0.3$ for the fiducial Pop III.1 model during these epochs.

entries.title: Dark Matter Model Implications of a Candidate Sub-halo Near the Sun, and the Data Needed to Discriminate Among Them
entries.abstract: Pulsar-timing accelerations point to a localized mass concentration near the Sun, consistent with a dark matter sub-halo. We work out what such an object implies for the nature of dark matter, organizing the implications by their observable effect: suppression or enhancement of structure formation, internal structure and survival after formation, and emission or scattering by the constituents. We discuss ultralight wave dark matter, thermal and nonthermal warm dark matter, dark acoustic oscillations and dark matter-baryon scattering, elastic and inelastic self-interactions, invisible decays with recoil, primordial black holes, indirect detection, and a possible connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy recoil candidate. We then ask what new data would discriminate among these models. The existing accelerations are measured outside the tidal radius, where they are blind to the interior mass distribution, to the object's velocity, and to the sub-halo population. We identify four routes that lift these degeneracies: accelerations measured inside the halo, which separate point-mass, cuspy, and cored profiles; lensing and accretion, which test whether the mass is compact; the morphology of annihilation or decay emission, which probes the inner profile; and a search for a comoving stellar population, which tests whether the object is dark and measures its velocity. We also contrast this program with pulsar-timing-array searches for transiting dark matter substructure, which probe vastly lighter objects through a different observable.

entries.title: A Shallow Phase-resolved Gamma-Ray Luminosity-Cutoff Energy Relation in Globular Cluster Millisecond Pulsars
entries.abstract: Globular clusters (GCs) provide dense stellar environments for investigating the high-energy emission of millisecond pulsars (MSPs). Using $\sim$17.3~yr of \textit{Fermi}-LAT Pass~8 data in the 0.1-500.0~GeV range, we study four MSPs that dominate, or contribute substantially to, the GeV $γ$-ray emission of their host GCs. Significant off-pulse $γ$-ray emission is detected from PSR~J1823$-$3021A, J1824$-$2452A, and J1835$-$3259B. For these sources, the cutoff energy, $E_{\rm cut}$, varies systematically with rotational phase and is positively correlated with the phase-resolved energy flux. Using the phase-resolved isotropic $γ$-ray luminosity ($L_γ$), we find $L_γ\propto E_{\rm cut}^α$ with $α=0.74^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. This slope is substantially shallower than that reported for field MSPs, $α=2.31^{+0.22}_{-0.25}$, and the $α=16/7\simeq2.29$ scaling expected for curvature radiation in the equatorial current sheet framework. The origin of the shallow relation remains uncertain, potentially reflecting cluster-associated $γ$-ray emission, differences in emission geometry and beaming, or limited photon statistics. Our results demonstrate that GC MSPs provide valuable targets for testing phase-resolved high-energy emission physics in dense stellar environments.

entries.title: TWIN-2: Timing Solar Radio Bursts between 180-350 MHz Against GOES and Aditya-L1 X-ray Detections
entries.abstract: We have conducted continuous solar observations for approximately two and half years using the Two-Element Interferometer (TWIN) at Gauribidanur Radio Observatory (RRI). During which several solar events have been detected. Our observational period coincides with the maximum events phase of the Solar Cycle 25, providing us opportunity to analyse the evolution of the solar activity. Our analysis of two and half years data show a clear increase in the occurrences of solar events, which is consistent with the expected rise in the solar activity towards the peak phase of the Solar Cycle 25. We further investigate the detected solar radio events using X-ray observations from the space based Aditya-L1 and the Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites (GOES) satellites. For the automated detection of SRBs, a machine learning suite has been trained. This also serves as an instrument for space weather monitoring. On the 7th of November 2025, a solar storm was detected by our pipeline in realtime. A brief overview of the data-processing pipeline, along with the RFI mitigation techniques employed to identify and characterize the solar events, is also presented. Observation data of two and a half years of TWIN is available for public access. The data has been used in student training programmes on solar radio data analysis, with students carrying out the analysis and contributing to the initial analysis of the detected events.

entries.title: Impact of Effective Nucleon Mass and Symmetry Energy on Nuclear Pasta Phases and the Unified Equation of State of Neutron Stars
entries.abstract: We investigate how the effective nucleon mass and symmetry energy affect pasta phase properties and the unified equation of state (EOS) of neutron stars. The nonuniform pasta structure is described within the self-consistent Thomas-Fermi approximation, while nucleonic interactions are treated in the relativistic mean-field framework with several typical parameter sets adopted. Our results indicate that the symmetry energy and its slope are crucial in determining the onset of pasta phases and their geometric configurations. In the high-density region where matter becomes uniform, the effective nucleon mass plays a dominant role. A larger effective nucleon mass tends to soften the EOS, which yields a smaller radius for a canonical $1.4 M_{\odot}$ neutron star and reduces the corresponding tidal deformability.

entries.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
entries.abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.

entries.title: False Periodicities in Repeating Fast Radio Bursts Caused by Burst Clustering
entries.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients with high brightness temperatures, but their physical origin remains uncertain. The association of FRB 200428 with a Galactic magnetar provides compelling evidence that at least some FRBs originate from magnetar-like systems. Nevertheless, periodic modulation associated with neutron-star rotation has not been robustly detected in extragalactic FRBs. Motivated by the reported 1.7 s periodicity in the active repeater FRB 20201124A, we conduct a systematic search for short-timescale periodicity in four highly active repeating FRB sources. We employ a sliding-window method that analyzes temporally adjacent bursts within restricted time intervals, allowing transient or intermittent periodic signals to be identified. The search yields apparent period candidates with nominal Poisson-calibrated significances comparable to that reported for the 1.7 s signal, although the inferred periods vary substantially among sources and observing windows. We then perform a nonparametric waiting-time randomization test, in which the observed waiting-time distribution is preserved while the temporal ordering is destroyed. The randomized sequences reproduce the main candidate-period structures seen in the data, demonstrating that these apparent periodicities can arise from the non-Poissonian waiting-time statistics rather than from a coherent periodic process. Rotation-modulated epidemic-type aftershock sequence simulations provide a complementary parametric illustration of the same effect. We therefore find no robust evidence for a short intrinsic periodicity in these data, and the reported 1.7 s signal is not uniquely distinguished from clustering-induced candidates. Robust periodicity searches must evaluate significance against null models that account for the observed waiting-time statistics and the full search procedure.

entries.title: New Candidate Activity Periods from FRB 20240209A and Repeating Fast Radio Burst Sources in the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
entries.abstract: Repeating fast radio burst (FRB) sources with periodic activity provide important constraints on FRB models invoking neutron-star precession, rotation, or orbital modulation in binary systems. Although a few FRB sources exhibit evidence of periodic behavior, it remains unclear whether periodic activity is a common underlying feature of repeating FRBs. Using a new FRB periodicity search pipeline introduced by A. B. Pearlman et al. (2026), which is optimized for sparse event-arrival-time data from FRB surveys, we search for activity periods in the burst arrival times from FRB 20240209A and repeating FRBs in the Second Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME)/FRB Catalog. For FRB 20240209A, we identify a new candidate activity period of 170.4 $\pm$ 4.7 days, with a trials-corrected statistical significance of 5.3$σ$. Our larger burst sample shows no evidence of the 128.5-day activity period previously reported for this source by A. Pal (2025). We also report candidate activity periods of 28.46 $\pm$ 0.08 days, 86.7 $\pm$ 0.5 days, and 36.4 $\pm$ 0.5 days for FRB 20190208A, FRB 20200926A, and FRB 20220529A, with trials-corrected statistical significances of 3.1$σ$, 4.0$σ$, and 3.5$σ$, respectively. All statistical significances are evaluated against a homogeneous (constant-rate) Poisson null hypothesis, and we caution that they may decrease under null models that incorporate burst clustering. Collectively, our results constitute the most comprehensive search for periodic activity in the repeating FRB population to date.

entries.title: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk $-$ new insights from GALAH DR4
entries.abstract: The non-equilibrium state of the Galactic disk has drawn extensive attention since ESA's \textit{Gaia} launch. Complex structure appears across a multi-parameter space of stellar abundances, ages, and kinematics. Using GALAH DR4, we investigate ridge and phase-spiral structures in chemical-abundance, phase ($v_i,x_i$), action--angle ($J_i,θ_i$), and frequency--action ($Ω_i,J_i$) spaces ($i=R,φ,z$). Our sample includes 333,412 disk stars with reliable chemodynamical data. In the $R$--$v_φ$ plane, ridges trace near-constant $J_φ$ tracks and show coherent variations in $θ_R$ and $θ_φ$. In $J_φ$--$J_R$, ridges are most prominent when encoded by $z_{\rm max}$ and preferentially associate with metal-rich, low-$α$ populations. In the solar neighbourhood ($R=7.2$--$9.2$\,kpc), we recover a clear phase spiral in $z$--$v_z$. Encoded in $v_φ$, $Ω_R$, or $Ω_φ$, one-armed spirals appear, whereas the $v_R$-encoded map shows a two-armed spiral. Projecting actions onto $z$--$v_z$ reveals residual spiral signatures in $J_R$ and $J_φ$, indicating that the phase spiral encodes in-plane orbital information. Both structures depend on age: ridges remain at similar locations with varying contrast, while the phase spiral is more tightly wound in younger and more loosely wound in older populations. Several ridges correspond in $J_φ$ to known moving groups, and excluding stars in all six moving-group regions makes the phase spiral less distinct in mean radial velocity maps. These links support interpreting ridges, phase spirals, and moving groups within a common phase-space dynamical framework. Combined with trends in orbital properties, age, and abundance, these findings suggest a common dynamical origin and distinct chemodynamical responses of a perturbed Galactic disk.

entries.title: Hard X-ray flux rope anchor points in the October 2024 X9 flare
entries.abstract: In recent studies, signatures of non-thermal hard X-ray (HXR) emission at the anchor point of erupting flux ropes were reported, suggesting that accelerated electrons trapped in the erupting flux ropes can reach the chromosphere and produce Bremsstrahlung emission there. We investigated the HXR sources observed during the impulsive phase of the X9-class flare SOL2024-10-03T12:18 from AR 13842 and assessed whether any of the HXR sources are associated with the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. We analysed the evolution and location of the flare ribbon sources and coronal dimmings to diagnose the eruption process by using multi-vantage point data from the Solar Orbiter and Earth-orbiting instruments. We combined this with a pre-eruption non-linear force-free magnetic field extrapolation to reconstruct the initial magnetic connectivity and compare it to the observed flare ribbons and dimming locations. The magnetic field extrapolation shows two flux ropes before the flare onset. Tether-cutting reconnection during the impulsive phase of the flare results in a larger erupting flux rope formed by the reconnection of the two pre-existing flux ropes. The Spectrometer/Telescope for Imaging X-rays on Solar Orbiter observes at least four distinct HXR sources: two flare footpoints and two additional outer sources at the anchor points of the erupting flux rope. These observations corroborate earlier speculations that non-thermal electrons trapped in the erupting flux rope precipitate along the field lines into the denser chromosphere.

entries.title: The origin of the apparent ULX deficit in NGC 3256
entries.abstract: Ultra-luminous X-ray (ULX) sources are bright, off-nuclear X-ray point sources, mostly associated with high-mass X-ray binaries (HMXBs), with a compact object accreting from a donor star at super-Eddington luminosities. Although their HMXB nature implies a connection to star formation processes, previous works have found that luminous infrared galaxies (LIRGs) appear to have a deficit of ULXs compared to their very high star formation rates (SFRs). Here, we analyze three Chandra observations of NGC 3256, a merging LIRG with SFR ~50-60 Msun/yr. Based on local scaling relations, it could be expected to host between 100-120 individual ULXs, which could have a non-negligible impact on the energetics and feedback processes of the galaxy. We aim to characterize all its detected X-ray point sources to determine if there is a ULX deficit in this galaxy. We also aim to explore the potential impact of host-galaxy obscuration and metallicity in said deficit. We characterize the luminosity of each X-ray point source in each Chandra observation, and use all observations to determine their potential ULX nature and the fraction of transient ULXs, as well as construct a ULX luminosity function for this galaxy. We find that the galaxy hosts 10-15 ULXs, making it one of the most ULX-rich galaxies known to date. While comparison with the ULX/SFR ratio of nearby galaxies predicted as many as ~100 ULXs, we show that, when accounting for its very high metallicity, NGC 3256 does not have a ULX deficit; and may even present an excess. While the high obscuration in LIRGs has previously been invoked to explain the ULX deficit, we conclude that it is not required to explain the ULX to SFR ratio in NGC 3256. If obscuration still plays a role, then LIRGs may actually be significantly more efficient at producing ULXs than normal galaxies (of the same metallicity), in disagreement with previous results.

entries.title: Neutral hydrogen in the Shapley Supercluster core II. Gas content and star formation in the filaments connecting the core
entries.abstract: We investigate the neutral atomic hydrogen (HI) content of galaxies across the Shapley Supercluster (SSC) at z = 0.048 by combining new deep MeerKAT L band observations of five filament pointings with archival MeerKAT Galaxy Cluster Legacy Survey observations of the supercluster core. Together with optical data from the Shapley Supercluster Survey, these observations provide a homogeneous view of galaxy evolution from the virialised cluster environment to the surrounding filaments. We compare the HI content, star formation activity, gas depletion timescales, and morphological properties of galaxies relative to the gas fraction and star forming main sequences. The global HI detection fraction increases from 30 per cent in the cluster centre to 45 per cent in the filaments. While HI detected galaxies in the cluster centre are dominated by transition zone systems, the filament population is shared nearly equally between star forming main sequence and transition zone detections, indicating ongoing environmental transformation. Their gas properties also differ: cluster galaxies exhibit progressively depleted HI reservoirs towards the red sequence, whereas filament galaxies remain primarily gas rich. Within the filaments, long HI depletion timescales exceeding the Hubble time are concentrated in specific populations, notably 71 per cent of transition zone and 57 per cent of gas rich detections, indicating the inefficient conversion of atomic gas into stars. The HI detected filament population is dominated by late type galaxies, while the underlying non detected population is primarily composed of early type systems, consistent with environmental pre processing before cluster infall.

entries.title: Gamma-Ray Bursts from Primordial Black Hole-Induced Neutron Star Collapse
entries.abstract: We show that the capture and subsequent endoparasitic consumption of a neutron star (NS) by a primordial black hole (PBH) can produce a short gamma-ray burst (GRB) without forming an accretion disk. During PBH-induced NS consumption, the NS spin is amplified through angular-momentum conservation and transfer from infalling matter, while flux freezing and a differential-rotation-driven dynamo amplify the magnetic field. We find that, for rapidly rotating millisecond pulsars (MSPs), these mechanisms can power short GRBs through magnetic dipole radiation and magnetic energy release. If asteroid-mass PBHs in the range $10^{-14}M_\odot$--$10^{-11}M_\odot$ constitute the dark matter, we estimate that searches of the Fermi-GBM archive and a future MeV gamma-ray mission such as COSI could detect these bursts. We also discuss possible multimessenger counterparts, including fast radio bursts powered by magnetic energy release, kilonovae and $511\,{\rm keV}$ line emission associated with centrifugally ejected neutron-rich matter, and gravitational waves from the rapid collapse and subsequent black-hole ringdown. Together, these signals probe complementary stages of PBH-induced NS consumption.

entries.title: Magnolia: a highly magnetized galaxy at redshift $z\simeq9$
entries.abstract: The theory of galactic magnetic field growth via dynamo action predicts that the interstellar medium (ISM) of early galaxies would remain virtually unmagnetized on large scales. However, recent observations of strong dust polarization in galaxies at redshifts $z\simeq2.6$ and $z\simeq5.6$ challenge this paradigm. If galaxies indeed host strong, large-scale, coherent magnetic fields at high-$z$, then galaxy evolution and current theories of magnetic field amplification in galaxies should be revisited. To address the full physical complexity of early magnetic field growth in galaxies, we have designed MAGNA SERRA, a suite of radiation-magneto-hydrodynamical (RMHD) cosmological zoom-in simulations with non-equilibrium chemistry. In this first paper from the MAGNA SERRA suite, we present Magnolia, a galaxy hosted in a $\simeq 10^{11}~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ dark matter halo simulated with RAMSES-RT with a $\simeq 10^4~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ mass ($\simeq 10 \,\mathrm{pc}$ spatial) resolution. We find that, at $z\simeq9$, Magnolia has a stellar mass of a few times $10^8~\mathrm{M}_\odot$ and is strongly magnetized, reaching a magnetic field of a few $μG$ and a plasma beta $β\simeq 0.1$ in the densest regions. This strong amplification occurs over a timescale of about 40~Myrs due to the highly dynamical nature of the galaxy, which creates strong compressions and shear. The power spectra of the magnetic and kinetic energies and the spectral energy transfer functions do not suggest dynamo action, but rather an initial magnetic field amplification through a large-scale compression, and a later re-organization of this field from small to large scales. Our findings show that strong galactic magnetization is possible at very high redshifts, which means that magnetic fields can play a dominant role throughout a galaxy's evolutionary history. (abridged)

entries.title: Spatio-Temporal Evolution of a Steady Transition Region Downflow above a Sunspot
entries.abstract: Super-Sonic Downflows (SSDs) are usually observed above sunspots as redshifted peaks in lower Transition Region (TR) spectral lines and can last from a few minutes to several hours. Utilising high-cadence, $\sim$3 hour long repeated-raster mode observations from Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), we investigate the spatio-temporal dynamics of such a downflow event above NOAA active region 12135. Triple Gaussian fitting to TR spectral lines, along with Non-Force Free Field (NFFF) extrapolation and Differential Emission Measure (DEM) analysis, is performed to study this event. Downflow is initially observed in both the umbral and penumbral regions. Over time, the penumbral downflow fades, while the umbral downflow strengthens and appears as a single structure initially but eventually splits into two spatial segments. The calculated average properties, including downflow speed, electron density, and mass flux for this event, align with established studies. Simultaneous evolution in overlying coronal loops is also observed using imaging data from the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA). DEM analysis of the coronal emission over the downflow region indicates corresponding changes in cool ($\log_{10}[T/\mathrm{K}] \in [5.5, 5.6]$) coronal plasma. As suggested by recurrent transient brightenings observed in the nearby region in coronal channels and the corresponding fan-spine magnetic topology identified from NFFF extrapolations, magnetic reconnection occurring in this region is proposed to be the cause of this evolution. Our analysis revealed that changes in the morphology of TR downflows are closely associated with evolution of overlying coronal loops.

entries.title: Superoutburst Precursors in the Faint SU UMa-type Dwarf Nova KSP-OT-201602a
entries.abstract: We present the discovery and photometric study of an SU UMa-type dwarf nova (DN) KSP-OT-201602a. Korea Microlensing Telescope Network Supernova Program data covered almost four years from 2016 to 2019 in BVI-bands for this field, and discovered this faint SU UMa-type DN. Two superoutbursts (SOs: S1 and S2) and two normal outbursts (NOs: N1 and N2) are observed of which peak brightnesses are V = 18.95 mag (S1), V = 18.69 mag (S2) and V = 19.37 mag (N1), V = 19.11 mag (N2). The phase dispersion minimization analysis on superhump of S1 gives the superhump period of 1.52 hr (= 91.2 minutes = 0.06333 days). The magnitude amplitudes for the SOs are 4.34 mag (S1) and 4.60 mag (S2), and those for the NOs are 3.98 mag (N1) and 4.18 mag (N2). The durations of the SOs are 11.39 days (S1) and 12.00 days (S2), and those for the NOs are 2.68 days (N1) and 3.38 days (N2). Clear evidence of a precursor is identified in S1 before the SO peak and this supports the hypothesis that precursor is an NO triggerring an SO and the superhump, while a potential precursor based on limited data is only observed in S2. While the amplitudes of the SOs appear typical for SU UMa-type DNe, their durations seem to be quite short which might require further model calculations in the future.

entries.title: Fast X-Ray Transients from Dense Circumstellar Material Shock Breakout and Cooling Emission
entries.abstract: In this Letter, we explore the soft X-ray shock breakout (SBO) and cooling emission of supernovae interacting with pre-explosion dense circumstellar material (CSM) shells as a subclass of extragalactic fast X-ray transients. For geometrically thin CSM shells, we find that the SBO luminosities span a range of a few $10^{43}-10^{45}\,{\rm{erg}}\,{\rm{s}}^{-1}$, with peak times typically $\lesssim10^4\,{\rm{s}}$, both of which are primarily determined by the light-travel effect. When the shell's outer radius is located at $\sim100-500\,R_\odot$, the SBO temperatures fall into the energy band covered by the current soft X-ray facilities. We derive analytic lightcurves for SBOs in dense CSM shells and explore how different physical parameters affect the observed lightcurves and the temperature evolution. Despite the multi-temperature nature of the emission caused by the light-travel effect leading to non-thermal-like spectra, we find that the time-resolved spectra within the limited soft X-ray band can still be well described by a blackbody model. This provides a natural explanation for the observed blackbody-like time-resolved spectra of soft X-ray SBO events. Our model can reproduce the observed X-ray lightcurves and temperature evolutions of the three known X-ray SBO events, EP260321a, XRF\,060218, and XRO\,080109, revealing a diversity in the properties of the dense CSM shells ejected by stripped-envelope progenitors before the explosion. Future discoveries of more soft X-ray SBO events by facilities such as Einstein Probe will provide opportunities for probing the episodic mass-loss history of massive stars in the final stages before core collapse.

entries.title: Strong Field Tidal Disruptions of Rotating Stars by Spinning Black Holes
entries.abstract: We study tidal disruptions of rotating solar-type stars by a rapidly spinning supermassive black hole with general-relativistic smoothed-particle hydrodynamics. To capture strong-field effects, we place the pericentre at a few gravitational radii of a black hole, and compare with weak-field encounters at a larger pericentre around a lighter black hole. We vary the black hole spin, the orbital inclination and the stellar rotation, using rigidly and differentially rotating stars with spin aligned, anti-aligned or perpendicular to the orbital angular momentum. In the strong field, the black hole spin decides whether a core survives on equatorial and inclined orbits, and stellar rotation reduces the surviving core in every partial disruption. At the larger pericentre, as in Newtonian studies, anti-aligned rotation instead protects the star from disruption. In both cases the tide reverses an anti-aligned spin just before pericentre. The outcome differs because in the strong field the tide keeps acting on the reversed core long after pericentre. Deep encounters leave cores spinning above break-up, which shed mass and angular momentum as they settle. Full disruptions approach the canonical fallback law, whereas the late-time slope of partial disruptions is not universal and is set by the debris energy distribution near the surviving core.

entries.title: Periodicities of small regular jet deviations in SS433 and their origin
entries.abstract: Based on the results of spectroscopic observations of SS433 conducted with the 2.5-m telescope at the Caucasian Mountain Observatory between 2020 and 2026, we study the deviations of the moving hydrogen and helium emission lines from their positions as predicted by the kinematic model of the jets' precessional motion. In these deviations, in addition to the previously known periodicities of $13^d.08$, $11^d.27$, $6^d.29$, and $5^d.83$, a new period of $3^d.08$ is identified. All observed periodicities are explained by a model in which the jet offsets occur in a fixed direction relative to the star-disk axis $\bf r$, and the magnitude of the offset is a function $a(μ)$, where $μ$ is the cosine of the angle between $\bf r$ and the direction of each jet. The odd terms of the power series expansion of $a(μ)$ in $μ$ yield periodicities of $6^d.29$, $5^d.83$, and $3^d.08$, with the jets shifting in opposite directions while remaining parallel. The even powers yield periodicities of $13^d.08$, $11^d.27$, and $4^d.14$ (the latter is not observed), with both jets shifting in the same direction, which was previously misinterpreted as a change in the jets' total velocity $β$. With the exception of the $6^d.29$ periodicity, all other displacements occur at an angle of $\approx120^\circ$ to $\bf r$. Superimposed on the regular variability are random deviations (jitter) in the jet directions, independent for the two jets, with $σ\lesssim1.\!\!^\circ5$.

entries.title: From a mass invariant in a gravo-turbulent medium to the characteristic mass of the star-forming cores
entries.abstract: The origin of the observed universality, or, say, the limited variations, of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) and its precursor, the prestellar core mass function (CMF), and thus of the characteristic mass of stars and cores, across a wide range of different galactic environments remains an open, fundamental problem in astrophysics. In this paper, we demonstrate that we can explain this property from gravity and turbulence only, using a mass time-invariant that remains valid for a broad class of turbulent flows throughout the star formation process. This mass invariant is entirely determined by the large-scale normalisation of the field of density fluctuations in the Galactic Interstellar Medium (ISM), induced by turbulence. Using high-resolution numerical simulations, we first verify that the temporal invariance of this quantity is preserved in a self-gravitating turbulent medium. Then, introducing a self-consistent model of the statistical properties of the density field in the self-gravitating multiphase turbulent ISM, we show that the universality of the characteristic mass of star-forming cores is imposed by this invariant together with the scaling of the Larson relations. Our model successfully predicts the characteristic mass of the cores in Milky Way-like star-forming regions, as well as in more extreme environments such as high-mass star-forming regions and massive early-type galaxies. This scenario suggests that the characteristic mass of the CMF, and then probably the characteristic stellar mass, originates from a universal, fundamental property of turbulence and is imprinted both by the very early stages of the star formation process in the gravo-turbulent interstellar medium, when the dynamics of the medium are still dominated by turbulence, and by the statistical properties of small-scale self-gravitating structures.

entries.title: Connecting Coronal Loop Scaling Laws and Kink Wave Heating: An Analytical and Numerical Study
entries.abstract: Turbulent dissipation of kink waves has been proposed as one of the mechanisms responsible for the observed high coronal temperatures. We test this hypothesis by examining the effect of this heating mechanism on coronal loops. The coronal loop static and dynamic behaviour is investigated under the assumption that the heating in the loop is primarily provided by kink wave dissipation. The heating term is borrowed from the recently developed UAWSoM model. Loop modelling is done in 1D using three different methods: one analytical following the principles first set in the RTV scaling laws, and two numerical: one based on the setup used to derive the RTVS scaling laws, and UAWSoM. We provide scaling laws and estimate density, temperature, and pressure, as well as kink wave heating rate and kink wave energy density needed to counteract energy loss by thermal conduction and radiative cooling. Estimates of kink wave energy density needed to heat the loop to 1 MK correspond to maximum velocity amplitudes of around 35 km s$^{-1}$ near the loop apex. Loop radius, density contrast and filling factor are found to affect the predictions significantly. The two numerical methods agree to a high degree. The analytical method predicts that $W_\textrm{k} \propto PL^{-2/3}$, while the two numerical methods show a wider range of scaling exponents which depend on the location in the loop. UAWSoM simulations suggest that loops may exhibit dynamic behaviour for a wide range of loop conditions, which may include thermal non-equilibrium cycles and periods of emerging and dissipating slow waves. Overall, estimates of kink wave energy density and scaling laws provide observational constraints on the importance of the proposed kink wave heating mechanism, with the current preliminary results suggesting that the uniturbulent kink wave heating may be a significant source of energy and heat in coronal loops.

entries.title: The gravitational wave candidate S251112cm: near-complete optical coverage with ATLAS, Pan-STARRS and the Vera C. Rubin Observatory
entries.abstract: On 2025 November 12, the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) network detected S251112cm, a compact binary merger candidate with a false alarm rate of one per four years at a luminosity distance of $93 \pm 27$ Mpc. The probability that the lighter component's mass lies below 1 $M_\odot$ is >99%, while the probability that either component lies at 1-3 $M_\odot$ is only 8%, leaving the nature of the progenitor system unclear. We present Pan-STARRS and ATLAS optical follow-up of the 90% localisation region, and quantify Vera C. Rubin Observatory target-of-opportunity observations. In the North, Pan-STARRS imaged 1084 deg$^2$ (65%) within 7 days to a median depth of 21.9 mag and ATLAS 1545 deg$^2$ (87%) within 14 days to 19.3 mag across both hemispheres; in the South, Rubin covered 849 deg$^2$ (36%) 2-10 days post-merger to median depths of 24.5 ($g$) and 23.5 ($i$) mag. They reported 173, 93 and 67 candidates respectively (269 unique), which we assess against AT 2017gfo-like kilonova and SN 1998bw-like broad-lined Type Ic supernova models using prior activity, host luminosity distance, photometric evolution and absolute magnitude. Eight survive, mainly for lack of distance information. Six of these lie in hosts fainter than any in a volume-limited comparison sample, suggesting they are background sources. AT 2025aimy declines too slowly for the AT 2017gfo-like model, and a VLT host spectrum places AT 2025alqe outside the LVK volume, leaving no convincing counterpart candidates. Pan-STARRS and Rubin together exclude both models in $\sim$80% of the 90% localisation volume: the deepest wide-area constraint on a subsolar-mass merger to date and, to our knowledge, the most complete optical coverage of a significant subsolar-mass candidate.

entries.title: The Silk Nebula Revisited: A Comment on Wu et al. (2026) and New Constraints from Archival Survey Spectroscopy
entries.abstract: Wu et al. (2026) used one LAMOST MRS-N plate to suggest that the Silk Nebula, a $17^\circ$-long \Oiii~$λ$5007 filament in Gemini, is possibly associated with a supernova remnant at a fiducial distance of $\sim$160\,pc. We test this against their published values and independent archival data. The \Ni\ airglow in their blue-arm spectrum lies at air, topocentric rest wavelengths, so their \Oiii\ velocities omit the heliocentric correction and are $10.1\pm1.0$\,\kms\ too high. Corrected and combined with DESI DR1 and SDSS spectra, \Oiii\ lies at \vhel\ $=+13.3\pm1.0$\,\kms, the velocity of \Nii\ and of the local warm ionized medium (WIM). Their \Ha\ velocities are 4.5--6.7\,\kms\ redder than \Nii. Their tabulated distances are in kpc, not units of 100\,pc, and kinematic distances carry no information in this direction. Their surface brightness exceeds independent measurements (1.4--2.5 rayleighs) by factors of 4.6--8.6. Their red-line shock criteria are met equally in their nebula-free background region and describe the WIM; their other remnant diagnostics do not constrain the filament. DESI and SDSS spectra show that the filament is Balmer-dark (\Oiii/\Hb\ $>11$) and \Oii-strong, with \ion{He}{2}/\Oiii\ $<0.026$; GALEX shows a coincident ultraviolet ridge, with no \Ha, \ion{H}{1}, dust or X-ray counterpart. These properties, and the lack of an ionizing source, exclude photoionization equilibrium and complete radiative shocks and match a column-truncated radiative shock of $\sim$80--120\,\kms\ seen edge-on, plausibly on the limb of the Monogem Ring at $\sim$250--320\,pc. Far-ultraviolet and deep optical spectroscopy, a two-epoch proper motion and high-ion absorption toward bracketing white dwarfs would be decisive.

entries.title: Disentangling star formation rate indicators in H-ATLAS galaxies: UV, FIR and radio diagnostics from energy-balance SED fitting
entries.abstract: We compare three star formation rate (SFR) tracers --- far-ultraviolet (FUV), far-infrared (FIR) and 1.4\,GHz radio emission --- for \Nsamp\ galaxies (median redshift 0.12) from the Herschel Astrophysical Terahertz Large Area Survey Data Release 1 catalogue, excluding quasars, AGN-dominated galaxies and unreliable redshifts. Energy-balance spectral energy distribution fitting with \textsc{cigale} gives their attenuations, dust luminosities and SFRs self-consistently. The FUV attenuation correlates strongly with FIR luminosity (Spearman $ρ=0.84$), largely through their common dependence on redshift (partial $ρ=0.57$ at fixed $z$), and more tightly with the infrared excess ($ρ=0.96$). The uncorrected UV SFR is over ten times below the FIR SFR for 67 per cent of the galaxies, and for all with $A_{\rm FUV}>4$\,mag. For 714 galaxies the FIRST 1.4\,GHz flux density is at the noise level and is treated as an upper limit; as detections, these values push the fits to unrealistically low dust temperatures. The 84 radio detections have a median $q_{\rm IR}$ of 2.51, close to the assumed 2.58. SFRs averaged over 10 and 100\,Myr differ by under 2 per cent, because the model star formation histories are smooth. Without access to high-performance computing, all galaxies were fitted at $z=0$, with distance-dependent quantities rescaled. This lowers dust temperatures by a factor of about $(1+z)$ and biases stellar masses and, at $z>0.2$, attenuations, but changes dust luminosities and SFRs by only a few hundredths of a dex. These fits, with 16.3 million models per galaxy, show what UV-to-radio SED modelling can deliver on modest hardware.

entries.title: Multiple blobs following a coronal mass ejection
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study a partial filament eruption, which generated a C4.1 class two-ribbon flare and a wide coronal mass ejection (CME) propagating in the northeast direction on 2023 March 20. The long, sigmoidal filament in active region 13258 is composed of two parts: the eruptive part and remaining part. Both of them are supported by magnetic flux ropes. The separation of two ribbons persist for ~12 hr, with the separation speeds decreasing from 0.26-5.62 to 0.13-0.53 km/s observed in H$α$ and 304 Å. A thin, curved current sheet follows the CME and extends in the northeast direction. Eight and seven bright blobs are found to move outward along the current sheet observed by SOHO/LASCO and STEREO-A/COR2, respectively. In LASCO images, the apparent speeds, lifetime, maximal height, and width of the blobs are 378-871 km/s, 7-84 minutes, 2.94-6.25\,$R_{\sun}$, and 38.8-225.4 Mm. In COR2 images, the apparent speeds, lifetime, maximal height, and width of the blobs are 336-712 km/s, 20-100 minutes, 4.09-7.61\,$R_{\sun}$, and 102.9-318.3 Mm. A positive correlation is found between the lifetime and maximal height, suggesting that blobs with longer lifetime propagate further from the solar surface. The total duration of blobs is >8 hr, which is consistent with ongoing flare reconnection manifested by persistent ribbon separation in the chromosphere. The aspect ratio (28-37) of the current sheet is probably larger than the critical value, suggesting that the blobs following the CME are possibly generated by tearing-mode instability of the current sheet.

entries.title: SN 2017gkk: A moderately luminous and fast evolving Type IIb supernova
entries.abstract: We present optical imaging (\textit{BVRI} bands) and low-resolution optical spectroscopic follow-up of Type IIb supernova SN~2017gkk that occurred in NGC~2748. These observations consist of 31 and 17 epochs of photometry and spectroscopy, spanning $\sim$\,218 days since the $V$-band peak. The light curve analysis infers that the SN reached maximum in $\sim$\,13~days after the explosion with an absolute magnitude of $M_\mathrm{V}$\,=\,--17.01\,$\pm$\,0.07 mag. The peak pseudo-bolometric luminosity of SN~2017gkk is $L_{\rm bol}=(8.37\pm0.19)\times10^{41}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. Between 25 and 80 days (after maximum), SN~2017gkk displays a fast decline rate of $2.35\pm0.06~\mathrm{mag\times(100d)^{-1}}$ in $V$-band. The photospheric phase spectra are dominated by an H$α$ P~Cygni profile (up to $\sim$\,69~days), which gradually faded and disappeared $\sim$\,90 days after the $V$-band maximum. The \ion{He}{1} lines subsequently emerged after $\sim$\,20 days and became dominant during the transition phase. The nebular phase spectra of SN~2017gkk indicate a relatively low-mass progenitor with $M_{\mathrm{preSN}}\gtrsim3\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\mathrm{ZAMS}}\approx\,12\,\mathrm{M_\odot}$, and it is likely in a binary system. The analytical modeling of the light curve infers a low ejecta mass of $M_{\mathrm{ej}}=1.38^{+0.48}_{-0.31}\, M_\odot$ with relatively lower explosion energy $E_\mathrm{KE}=0.69_{-0.17}^{+0.25}\times10^{51}\,\mathrm{erg}$ and a synthesized $^{56}$Ni mass of $M_{\mathrm{Ni}}=0.076_{-0.024}^{+0.032}\, M_\odot$.

entries.title: Feature redundancy, redshift, and class-prior effects in SDSS--WISE photometric classification
entries.abstract: Photometric classification of galaxies, quasars, and stars is important for future imaging surveys, but reported performance depends on the engineered features, spectroscopic redshift, class priors, and the sample used for evaluation. We separate these four factors on 3.65 million SDSS DR17--WISE sources, train five classifiers on twelve feature scenarios. We combine a four-method feature ranking, raw-only baselines, grouped importance, and a paired bootstrap, with explicit priors, magnitude shifts, and WISE/redshift ablations. With spectroscopic redshift the tuned Random Forest reaches a macro-$F_1$ of $0.9834$; without it, 10 raw features give $0.9507$ and 24 features $0.9551$.
